kill_argument: The paper now says what it found, but what it found is thin. Its one confirmatory calibration test (H1) is relative, and it uses an estimator whose noise floor (0.01-0.04) exceeds the 0.005 margin. Its 'contradicted' verdict comes down to default LR being miscalibrated on two datasets where a linear model fits poorly, which is the textbook caveat to the textbook result. Both isotonic verdicts turn on electricity, whose random splits straddle neighbouring half-hours; the one check meant to test that measured drift instead, so their basis is open. Everything else is descriptive. A referee would call this a careful null-ish report on four datasets, not evidence on whether recalibration helps. What I attacked that held: the 12 paper-r1 findings are fixed in the files. Every Sec. 6 'Recorded' pointer matches a log line and plan.json hash, and the current plan.json sha256 equals the 12:57Z log line. The Manokhin Appendix A ranks match the arXiv figure. All 72 new machine-epsilon macros map to the right describe keys. main.pdf is built from the current tex. No run, code or result file changed since the results gate. validate --strict passes. What remains is four minor wording and disclosure-accuracy points.

findings.text: The abstract presents the debiased ECE as corroboration: 'a debiased estimator, reported descriptively, points the same way on every dataset'. The body says the opposite about what that agreement is worth. The estimator keeps about 0.6 of any floor difference with its sign, so its agreement 'is not confirmation' (Sec. 3.4, Sec. 4.1, Table 3 caption). It also moves adult from inconclusive to holds. This was conceded at code-r1 F2: the replication licence was dropped because ece_db agreement is close to vacuous. A reader of the abstract alone takes the sentence as a robustness check. Remedy (cheap): delete the clause, or add 'which, since it keeps most of any floor difference, is not independent confirmation'.

findings.ruling: Abstract (main.tex lines 56-58) now says the debiased ECE gives the same signs but keeps most of any floor difference, so its agreement is not independent confirmation. This matches Sec. 3.4, Sec. 4.1 and Table 3. No replacement reassurance was added.

findings.text: Related work attributes to Manokhin and Gronhaug (2026) per-dataset counts that the cited paper does not report: 'isotonic lowered the mean log-loss of random forests on 18 of 30 datasets but that of HistGradientBoostingClassifier on only 4 of 30'. sources/notes.md says Appendix A 'gives no per-dataset breakdown'. The counts are the Scout's own summary of the authors' released archive, made by a scratchpad script that was not kept and is not a logged run (sources.json manokhin2026 note). They are also selective. The same tabulation gives Brier counts, and Brier is this paper's own H2 metric: isotonic was better for RF on 13 of 30 and for HGB on 14 of 30. On Brier, the RF/HGB contrast the sentence draws disappears. Claim c-manokhin-archive carries the same attribution. Remedy (cheapest): drop the sentence and keep the Appendix A ranks. Otherwise, label it as the crew's tabulation of the released results, back it with a logged data-prep run that hashes the archive, and report Brier beside log-loss.

Expected log-loss rank: rf 67.69 to rf.isotonic 59.19 (improved); hgb 38.76 to 57.37 and gbc 30.38 to 62.85 (worsened); rf.platt 43.45, hgb.platt 42.88 and gbc.platt 45.57 are each ahead of isotonic. The claim holds.

findings.text: The AI-use statement misreports the code review. It says 'The code review passed with no critical finding before any analysis run', and lists code round 1 among stages whose 'last round ... passed with minor findings still open'. In fact code-r1's verdict was revise, with two major findings open (F1 one-hot width assertion; F2 ece_db replication licence) and one minor. There was no code round 2. main started at 07:43:43Z, under two minutes after code-r1 (created 07:42:00Z) and 33 s after the re-run of unit-tests finished. The Reviewer first checked the fixes at results-r1 (08:11Z), after all five analysis runs. Sec. 3.6 likewise says only that 'the Reviewer checked the code against the approved method'. The plan's bar (no open critical finding before analysis; analysis_plan[3]) was met, so this is a disclosure error, not a protocol breach. But the AI-use statement is the record of oversight and must be exact. Remedy: state the verdict (revise; 2 major, 1 minor), that F1 was fixed and F2/F3 narrowed before main without a second code review, and that results-r1 verified them.

findings.text: The abstract's H1 sentence ('is contradicted: RF scored lower, with RF-minus-LR differences of ... on bank-marketing and ... on phoneme') omits that H1 held on electricity (0.0270 [0.0232, 0.0308]) and was inconclusive on adult. Read alone, 'RF scored lower' sounds general. Remedy: 'RF scored lower on two of four datasets; the published direction held on electricity'.
findings.response: Abstract's H1 sentence now says RF scored lower on two of four datasets, the published direction held on electricity (with its interval) and adult was inconclusive.
findings.ruling: The abstract's H1 sentence now says RF scored lower on two of four datasets, that the published direction held on electricity (with its interval), and that adult was inconclusive.

findings.text: 'Platt scaling, fitted on the logit, changed little' (Sec. 4.4) and 'Platt scaling on the logit changed little throughout' (Sec. 5) contradict the paper's own numbers. For RF on electricity, Platt minus none was -0.0029 [-0.0032, -0.0027]. That is the same size as isotonic's -0.0028, which the paper treats as the one H2a 'holds' beyond the margin. For HGB on electricity it was -0.0008 [-0.0010, -0.0006]. Remedy: 'changed little except for the tree models on electricity'.
findings.response: Sec. 4.4 and Sec. 5 now say Platt changed little except for the tree models on electricity, where for RF it matched isotonic's change (H2a's one holds).
findings.ruling: The text now carries the qualifier I proposed ('except for the tree models on electricity'). My remedy was incomplete: RF on phoneme is a second exception. That is raised as new F13, not reopened here.

findings.text: The title promises more than the tests deliver. 'Are Default Tabular Classifiers Calibrated, and Does Isotonic Recalibration Help?' invites absolute answers. The confirmatory test of calibration is relative (RF vs LR) and estimator-bound. The isotonic tests end inconclusive and no difference, with both verdicts resting on electricity. Remedy: a title that names what was tested, e.g. 'Random Forest versus Logistic Regression Calibration and Isotonic Recalibration under scikit-learn Defaults: Pre-Specified Tests on Four OpenML Datasets'.
findings.response: Title narrowed to 'Random Forest versus Logistic Regression on a Plug-in ECE, and Isotonic Recalibration of Tree Ensembles, under scikit-learn Defaults: Pre-Specified Tests on Four OpenML Datasets'.
findings.ruling: The title now names the relative, estimator-bound RF-versus-LR test and isotonic recalibration of tree ensembles under defaults, on four OpenML datasets. It no longer promises absolute answers.

findings.text: 'Platt scaling, fitted on the logit, changed little except for the tree models on electricity' (Sec. 4.4) and 'changed little except for RF and HGB on electricity, where for RF it lowered the Brier score by as much as isotonic regression did' (Sec. 5) leave out a second case. For RF on phoneme, Platt minus none was -0.0009 [-0.0017, -0.0001]. That is about the 0.001 margin, its interval excludes zero, and it is a larger fall than isotonic's H2a phoneme change of -0.0007 [-0.0018, 0.0005], which was inconclusive. For HGB, Platt's changes on bank-marketing and phoneme (-0.0005, both intervals excluding zero) are the same size as the isotonic H2b changes. My paper-r1 F7 remedy was too narrow. Remedy (cheap; the macros exist): 'changed LR's Brier score little; for RF it lowered it by about the margin on electricity and phoneme, at least as much as isotonic did', or quote the phoneme RF interval.

findings.text: The AI-use statement says the clean rerun 'downloaded the data again rather than reusing it', and Sec. 3.7 says 'with the data downloaded again'. The cold download was a separate, unlogged fetch_data.py run that matched the 4 CSV hashes and the 32 fetch-data metrics. replication.json's reuse_data:false covers only the recorded outputs. The data are the same, so no number is affected, but the AI-use statement is the record of oversight and should be exact. Remedy: 'rebuilt the data from the md5-checked download cache; a separate cold download from OpenML matched every data hash'.

findings.text: The new machine-epsilon summary sentence is selective: 'At this clipping constant isotonic's log-loss advantage over no recalibration is larger on adult, and on phoneme the two are equal'. It leaves out electricity, the dataset that carries H2a's only holds. There the advantage halves, from 0.010 (0.323 to 0.313) at 1e-6 to 0.005 (0.326 to 0.321) at machine epsilon. It also leaves out bank-marketing, where the advantage grows from 0.002 to 0.007. All the levels are printed as macros, so nothing is hidden, but the sentence picks two of four. Remedy: 'larger on adult and bank-marketing, smaller on electricity, unchanged on phoneme', or drop the comparison.
findings.response: The machine-epsilon sentence now covers all four datasets: isotonic's RF log-loss advantage is larger on adult and bank-marketing, smaller on electricity, unchanged on phoneme.
